question: What is DispatcherServlet in Spring MVC?
title: DispatcherServlet in Spring MVC — Front Controller Pattern
direct_answer: **DispatcherServlet** is Spring MVC's **front controller** — a single servlet that intercepts every incoming HTTP request and routes it to the correct handler (controller method). It implements the Front Controller design pattern. Spring Boot auto-configures it at URL pattern `/`.

interviewer_intent.testing: Understanding of Spring MVC request processing pipeline
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking controllers directly handle HTTP — DispatcherServlet is the entry point for all requests
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Walk through the full request lifecycle: DispatcherServlet → HandlerMapping → Controller → MessageConverter → Response

sections.title: DispatcherServlet Request Flow
sections.content:
```
HTTP Request
    ↓
DispatcherServlet (front controller — intercepts ALL requests)
    ↓
HandlerMapping (finds which controller method handles this URL)
    ↓
HandlerAdapter (calls the controller method)
    ↓
Controller method (business logic → calls service)
    ↓
[For REST]: HttpMessageConverter (serializes return value to JSON)
[For MVC]: ViewResolver (finds template from view name)
    ↓
HTTP Response
```

sections.title: DispatcherServlet Key Facts
sections.content:
- **Front Controller pattern**: Single entry point for all requests — central request routing
- **Auto-configured**: Spring Boot registers DispatcherServlet at `/` automatically via `DispatcherServletAutoConfiguration`
- **`HandlerMapping`**: Maps URL + HTTP method to controller method (e.g., `RequestMappingHandlerMapping`)
- **`HandlerAdapter`**: Calls the handler — handles method parameters, return values
- **`ViewResolver`**: Resolves view name to template (e.g., `"users"` → `templates/users.html`)
- **`HttpMessageConverter`**: Converts return objects to HTTP response body (JSON via Jackson)
- **Multiple DispatcherServlets**: Possible but rare — Spring Boot creates one by default
- **Servlet context**: DispatcherServlet has its own Spring application context inheriting from root context

sections.title: How to Answer in an Interview
sections.content: DispatcherServlet is the heart of Spring MVC. It's a single servlet that sits at the front and intercepts every HTTP request that comes into your application — this is the Front Controller design pattern. When a request arrives, DispatcherServlet consults HandlerMapping to find out which controller method is responsible for that URL and HTTP method combination. It then calls that method using a HandlerAdapter. If the method returns data for a REST response, a MessageConverter — usually Jackson — serializes it to JSON. If it returns a view name for a traditional MVC app, a ViewResolver finds the corresponding template. Spring Boot auto-configures all of this for you — you just write controllers.

question: What is HandlerMapping in Spring MVC?
title: HandlerMapping in Spring MVC — URL to Controller Method Resolution
direct_answer: **`HandlerMapping`** is the Spring MVC component that determines which controller method should handle an incoming HTTP request based on URL path, HTTP method, headers, and parameters. `RequestMappingHandlerMapping` is the default implementation — it scans `@RequestMapping` annotations.

interviewer_intent.testing: Depth of Spring MVC internal knowledge beyond just annotations
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not knowing HandlerMapping exists — thinking Spring 'magically' routes requests
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention multiple HandlerMapping beans and their priority order

sections.title: HandlerMapping Role
sections.content:
When DispatcherServlet receives `GET /api/users/1`, it asks `HandlerMapping`:
**"Which method handles this request?"**

`RequestMappingHandlerMapping` scans all `@Controller` / `@RestController` beans at startup, builds a map of `{URL pattern + HTTP method} → controller method`, and consults this map for each request.

Result: `UserController.getById(Long id)` method + any applicable interceptors.

sections.title: HandlerMapping Implementations
sections.content:
- **`RequestMappingHandlerMapping`** (default): Scans `@RequestMapping` and method-level annotations; used for all @Controller methods
- **`BeanNameUrlHandlerMapping`**: Maps URL to bean name (legacy pattern)
- **`SimpleUrlHandlerMapping`**: Manual URL → handler mapping (XML config era)
- **Priority**: Multiple HandlerMappings ordered by priority — Spring checks them in order
- **`HandlerExecutionChain`**: HandlerMapping returns this — contains the handler + any matched interceptors
- **Interceptors**: `HandlerInterceptor` beans registered with HandlerMapping — run before/after each request
- **Ambiguous mappings**: If two methods match the same URL+method, Spring throws `AmbiguousHandlerMappingException` at startup

sections.title: How to Answer in an Interview
sections.content: HandlerMapping is the component in Spring MVC responsible for figuring out which controller method handles a given request. At application startup, RequestMappingHandlerMapping — the main implementation — scans all your @Controller and @RestController beans and builds a lookup table mapping URL patterns and HTTP methods to controller methods. When a request comes in, DispatcherServlet asks HandlerMapping for the handler, and it returns the matching controller method along with any registered interceptors. If you define two controller methods with the same URL and HTTP method, Spring throws an AmbiguousHandlerMappingException at startup, which is a helpful fail-fast behavior.

question: What happens when a Spring Boot application starts with Spring MVC?
title: Spring MVC Auto-Configuration at Startup — What Spring Boot Does
direct_answer: On startup, Spring Boot auto-configures: registers `DispatcherServlet` at `/`, creates `RequestMappingHandlerMapping` by scanning all `@Controller` beans, configures `Jackson` as the default JSON `HttpMessageConverter`, sets up `ViewResolvers` for Thymeleaf if present, and registers default exception handlers.

interviewer_intent.testing: Understanding of Spring Boot auto-configuration for Spring MVC
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not knowing why adding spring-boot-starter-web is enough to get a working REST API
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention WebMvcAutoConfiguration and how @EnableWebMvc overrides it

sections.title: Spring MVC Startup Sequence
sections.content:
Adding `spring-boot-starter-web` dependency triggers Spring Boot's `WebMvcAutoConfiguration`:

1. **DispatcherServlet** registered at `/`
2. **HandlerMappings** created and all `@Controller` beans scanned
3. **Jackson** `ObjectMapper` configured — JSON serialization for all `@RestController` responses
4. **Validation** auto-configured if `spring-boot-starter-validation` present
5. **Error handling** via `BasicErrorController` at `/error`
6. **Static resources** served from `/static`, `/public`, `/resources`, `/META-INF/resources`
7. **Thymeleaf** ViewResolver configured if `spring-boot-starter-thymeleaf` present

sections.title: Auto-Configuration Components
sections.content:
- **`WebMvcAutoConfiguration`**: Main auto-config class — configures the whole Spring MVC stack
- **`DispatcherServletAutoConfiguration`**: Registers the DispatcherServlet bean
- **`HttpMessageConvertersAutoConfiguration`**: Adds Jackson, JAXB converters
- **`ErrorMvcAutoConfiguration`**: Sets up default error handling at `/error`
- **`@EnableWebMvc`**: Overrides auto-configuration — use only if you need full manual control; otherwise let Boot handle it
- **`WebMvcConfigurer`**: Interface to customize auto-configuration without overriding it completely
- **`application.properties`**: `spring.mvc.format.date`, `spring.web.resources.static-locations`, etc.

sections.title: How to Answer in an Interview
sections.content: When a Spring Boot application starts with spring-boot-starter-web, Spring Boot's auto-configuration does a lot of setup automatically. The main class is WebMvcAutoConfiguration — it registers DispatcherServlet at the root URL, scans all @Controller and @RestController beans to build handler mappings, configures Jackson for JSON serialization, sets up default error handling at /error, and serves static resources from classpath. This is why you can just write a @RestController and have a working REST API without any XML configuration. If you need to customize Spring MVC behavior, you implement WebMvcConfigurer — that lets you add interceptors, CORS config, and formatters while keeping all the auto-configuration. You'd only use @EnableWebMvc if you want full manual control.

question: What is a HandlerInterceptor in Spring MVC?
title: HandlerInterceptor in Spring MVC — Pre and Post Processing
direct_answer: **`HandlerInterceptor`** intercepts HTTP requests at the Spring MVC layer — before and after controller method execution. Used for cross-cutting concerns: authentication checks, logging, timing, rate limiting. It's Spring MVC's equivalent of a filter but operates within the Spring context.

interviewer_intent.testing: Knowledge of Spring MVC's interceptor mechanism for cross-cutting concerns
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Confusing Spring HandlerInterceptor with Servlet Filter — both intercept requests but at different layers
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Explain the three methods: preHandle (before), postHandle (after method, before response), afterCompletion (after response)

sections.title: HandlerInterceptor Methods
Interceptor vs Filter
sections.content:
- **`HandlerInterceptor`**: Spring MVC layer — runs AFTER DispatcherServlet, has access to `handler` (controller method info)
- **Servlet `Filter`**: Servlet container layer — runs BEFORE DispatcherServlet, no Spring context awareness
- **`preHandle`**: Return `false` to abort the request (e.g., unauthorized)
- **`postHandle`**: Only called if controller succeeded — can modify ModelAndView for MVC views
- **`afterCompletion`**: Always called — good for resource cleanup, final logging
- **Register interceptors**: Implement `WebMvcConfigurer.addInterceptors()` to register
- **URL patterns**: Can restrict which URLs interceptor applies to: `addInterceptors().addPathPatterns("/api/**")`
- **Use cases**: Authentication, logging, request timing, locale/theme resolution

sections.title: How to Answer in an Interview
sections.content: HandlerInterceptor is Spring MVC's mechanism for cross-cutting concerns like logging, authentication checks, and request timing. It runs at the Spring layer after DispatcherServlet has identified the handler, unlike Servlet filters which run before DispatcherServlet. HandlerInterceptor has three methods: preHandle runs before the controller method and returns a boolean — return false to reject the request; postHandle runs after the controller but before the response is written; afterCompletion runs after the complete request is done, including response. You register interceptors by implementing WebMvcConfigurer and overriding addInterceptors. A key difference from Servlet filters: interceptors have access to the Spring context and know which controller method is being called.

question: What is ViewResolver in Spring MVC?
title: ViewResolver in Spring MVC — Resolving View Names to Templates
direct_answer: **`ViewResolver`** resolves a view name string returned by a `@Controller` method into an actual view template. For example, `InternalResourceViewResolver` maps `"users"` to `/WEB-INF/views/users.jsp`. `ThymeleafViewResolver` maps it to `templates/users.html`.

interviewer_intent.testing: Understanding of how @Controller view resolution works
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking ViewResolver is used in REST APIs — it's only for traditional MVC with view templates
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention ContentNegotiatingViewResolver and that @RestController bypasses ViewResolver entirely

sections.title: ViewResolver Flow
sections.content:
When a `@Controller` method returns `"users"` (a string view name):
1. DispatcherServlet passes `"users"` to `ViewResolver`
2. ViewResolver looks up the template: `templates/users.html` (Thymeleaf) or `WEB-INF/views/users.jsp` (JSP)
3. Template engine renders HTML by merging template + Model data
4. HTML sent as HTTP response

For `@RestController`: ViewResolver is bypassed — the return object goes directly to `HttpMessageConverter`

sections.title: ViewResolver Implementations
sections.content:
- **`ThymeleafViewResolver`** (Spring Boot default with Thymeleaf): Resolves to `classpath:/templates/{name}.html`
- **`InternalResourceViewResolver`**: Classic JSP — maps to WEB-INF paths with prefix/suffix
- **`ContentNegotiatingViewResolver`**: Selects the best ViewResolver based on Accept header or URL extension
- **`BeanNameViewResolver`**: Maps view name to Spring bean
- **Spring Boot auto-config**: ThymeleafViewResolver auto-configured when `spring-boot-starter-thymeleaf` is on classpath
- **Prefix/suffix config** (InternalResourceViewResolver):
  `spring.mvc.view.prefix=/WEB-INF/views/`, `spring.mvc.view.suffix=.jsp`
- **REST note**: `@RestController` / `@ResponseBody` short-circuits ViewResolver — response written directly

sections.title: How to Answer in an Interview
sections.content: ViewResolver is used in traditional Spring MVC apps where controllers return view names. When your @Controller method returns the string 'users', DispatcherServlet passes that to the ViewResolver to find the actual template file. If you're using Thymeleaf, the ThymeleafViewResolver looks for templates/users.html. If you're using JSP, InternalResourceViewResolver uses the configured prefix and suffix to construct the path. ViewResolver is only relevant for @Controller methods returning view names — when you use @RestController or add @ResponseBody, the return value goes straight to HttpMessageConverter and ViewResolver is bypassed entirely. Spring Boot auto-configures the appropriate ViewResolver based on what template engine dependency you have on the classpath.

question: What is HttpMessageConverter in Spring MVC?
title: HttpMessageConverter in Spring — Serialization and Deserialization
direct_answer: **`HttpMessageConverter`** converts Java objects to HTTP response bodies (serialization) and HTTP request bodies to Java objects (deserialization). `MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter` handles JSON. Spring Boot auto-configures it when Jackson is on the classpath.

interviewer_intent.testing: Understanding of how @RequestBody and @ResponseBody actually work
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking Jackson 'just works' without understanding the MessageConverter chain
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Explain content negotiation — Spring selects the converter based on Accept and Content-Type headers

sections.title: HttpMessageConverter Role
sections.content:
**Deserialization** (`@RequestBody`):
```
HTTP Request body (JSON bytes)
    ↓ HttpMessageConverter reads JSON → creates Java object
Controller method parameter
```

**Serialization** (`@ResponseBody` / `@RestController`):
```
Controller return value (Java object)
    ↓ HttpMessageConverter writes Java → JSON bytes
HTTP Response body
```

Spring selects the converter based on `Content-Type` (request) and `Accept` header (response).

sections.title: Message Converter Types
sections.content:
- **`MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter`**: JSON — auto-configured when `jackson-databind` on classpath
- **`StringHttpMessageConverter`**: For `String` return type → `text/plain`
- **`ByteArrayHttpMessageConverter`**: Binary data
- **`Jaxb2RootElementHttpMessageConverter`**: XML — requires `jackson-dataformat-xml` or JAXB
- **Content negotiation**: Client sends `Accept: application/json` → Spring picks Jackson converter
- **`Content-Type` header**: Client sends `Content-Type: application/json` → Spring uses Jackson to read `@RequestBody`
- **Jackson ObjectMapper**: Underlying Jackson instance — customizable via `@Bean ObjectMapper`
- **`@JsonIgnore`**: Jackson annotation to exclude field from JSON serialization

sections.title: How to Answer in an Interview
sections.content: HttpMessageConverter is what handles the actual conversion between Java objects and HTTP bodies. When your @RestController method returns a User object, Spring picks the right MessageConverter based on what the client asked for in the Accept header. If the client wants JSON — which is the default — Spring uses MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter to serialize the User object to JSON bytes. In the other direction, when you have @RequestBody on a controller parameter, Spring uses the same converter to deserialize the incoming JSON into a Java object. Spring Boot automatically configures Jackson as the JSON converter when it's on the classpath. You can customize Jackson's behavior by defining an ObjectMapper bean with your preferred settings.
